texto: In the distended conversation we usually hear * weden dem Wetter * or * Trotz dem Lärm * with dativa. In formal reactions and official language tests B1 / B2, the use of the dativa is considered a style incorriguation; the culta norm requires without exception the genitive (**wegen des Wetters**, **trotz des Lärms**).

frases.de: Seid ihr trotz des Flugausfalls noch rechtzeitig zur Eröffnung eingetroffen?
frases.es: ¿Habéis llegado a tiempo para la inauguración a pesar de la cancelación del vuelo?
frases.en: Have you arrived in time for the opening despite the cancellation of the flight?

frases.de: Ja, wir haben wegen der widrigen Wetterlage sofort den Schnellzug gebucht.
frases.es: Sí, debido a las adversas condiciones meteorológicas reservamos de inmediato el tren de alta velocidad.
frases.en: Yes, due to the adverse weather conditions we immediately reserve the high-speed train.

frases.de: Eine kluge Entscheidung. Wegen eines Streiks der Piloten war der Flughafen blockiert.

frases.en: A sensible decision. The airport was blocked by a pilot strike.

bloques.pregunta: What case does the standard standard cults after the cause preposition «wegen» require?

opciones.texto: Genitive case singular or plural according to the noun that accompanies it.
opciones.explicacion: «wegen» is a preposition that governs genitive in the standard German standard.

opciones.texto: Dative case only when the subject is an individual person.
opciones.explicacion: The Dativa after «wegen» is a colloquial feature not accepted in the formal standard.

opciones.texto: Direct indicative case to indicate the spatial direction of the displacement.
opciones.explicacion: «wegen» expresses abstract cause or motive, never spatial translation.

bloques.frase: Trotz ___ intensiven Bemühungen konnte der Termin nicht eingehalten werden.

opciones.explicacion: Plural genitive of the given article: «trotz der Bemühungen».
«den» is plural dative, typical of the colloquial variant but not of the formal standard.
«des» is the form of singular masculine or neutral genitive.

bloques.pregunta: What does this official notice report?
bloques.frase: Wegen des anhaltenden Streiks blieben die Werkstätten der Bahn geschlossen.

opciones.texto: As a result of the long strike, the railway workshops remained closed.
opciones.explicacion: «wegen des anhaltenden Streiks» expresses the cause that caused the closure by genitive.

opciones.texto: Despite the strike, the railway operators kept all the workshops open.
La huelga fue convocada por los empleados que reclamaban la reapertura inmediata.
opciones.explicacion: It does not explain the demands of the strike, but its operational effects.

bloques.frase: Der Bus fuhr ___ dichten Schneefalls pünktlich an der Haltestelle ab.

opciones.explicacion: «trotz» requires masculine singular: «trotz des Schneefalls» genitive.
«trotz dem» is a non-standard dialectal or colloquial formulation.
«wegen» would indicate cause («because of the snow came out on time»), which lacks logical sense.

bloques.pregunta: What logical nuance does «trotz des Regens» differ from «wegen des Regens»?

opciones.texto: «trotz» points to a overcome obstacle (concession), while «wegen» introduces the direct causing motive.
opciones.explicacion: «trotz» contrasts a fact with its expected consequence; «wegen» justifies the reason for the fact.

opciones.texto: «trotz» solo se emplea para fenómenos meteorológicos y «wegen» para relaciones humanas.
opciones.explicacion: Both prepositions are used indistinctly for any conceptual field.

opciones.texto: No existe ninguna distinción semántica; ambos términos son sinónimos absolutos e intercambiables.
opciones.explicacion: They have opposite logical orientations (direct cause against concessional opposition).

bloques.traduccion: Because of the dense fog, the plane landed late.
bloques.explicacion: Preposition of genitive + declinated core + verb and subject investment.

intro: In the formal, academic and journalistic record of level B1.2, the causal and concessional prepositions **wegen** (because of) and **trotz** (despite) necessarily govern genitive case.
